raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`DeepSeekV3Detector` (`deepseekv3`) scans model output with patterns that go quadratic when the closing tokens never arrive:

1. `parse_streaming_increment` runs ``re.search(r"<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>(.*)<｜tool▁sep｜>(.*)\n```json\n(.*)\n```.*")`` over the **whole buffer on every chunk**. With repeated `<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>` / `<｜tool▁sep｜>` tokens and no JSON fence, each call backtracks over every begin/sep pair.
2. `detect_and_parse` uses `re.findall(begin.*?end)`, rescanning to the end from every begin token, then the same greedy detail pattern on each block.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 130 KB, one streaming call | 8.3 – 9.4 s | ~0 |
| 31 KB stream in 64-char (multi-token / MTP) chunks | 0.65 s worst chunk, **85 s total** | 0.01 s total |
| 130 KB, non-stream | 5.7 s | ~0 |

Tool-call parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so one such response stalls every in-flight request. Found with an Atheris fuzzing harness that records per-input parse time.

## Modifications

- `_iter_call_blocks`: a linear `str.find` scan for `begin ... end` blocks. It is used in `detect_and_parse` and when trimming the completed block from the stream buffer.
- `_greedy_chain_search(text, a, b, c, d)`: computes the same groups as `re.search(a(.*)b(.*)c(.*)d, DOTALL)` for literal tokens from a few `find` / `rfind` calls. A match can only start at the first `a`, and the greedy groups take the last `d`, then the last `c` ending before it, then the last `b` ending before that. It replaces both greedy patterns. The unused `func_call_regex` / `func_detail_regex` attributes and `import re` are removed.
- Regression test in `TestDeepSeekV3Detector` (fails on `main`, passes here).

## Accuracy Tests

- `_greedy_chain_search` vs both original patterns on 300k random token strings: identical.
- Differential test of `main` vs patched detector (20k random + 20k mutated well-formed inputs, streaming under random re-chunking and non-streaming): **0 mismatches** (11.5k produced parsed calls).
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/`: 630 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above.

Related: #42573 – #42591 (same issue class in other tool-call parsers).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 import json
 import logging
-import re
-from typing import List
+from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
 
 from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Tool
 from sglang.srt.function_call.base_format_detector import BaseFormatDetector
@@ -16,6 +15,50 @@
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
 
+_CALL_BEGIN = "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>"
+_CALL_END = "<｜tool▁call▁end｜>"
+_SEP = "<｜tool▁sep｜>"
+_JSON_OPEN = "\n```json\n"
+_JSON_CLOSE = "\n```"
+
+
+def _greedy_chain_search(
+    text: str, a: str, b: str, c: str, d: str
+) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str, str, int]]:
+    # Linear equivalent of re.search(a(.*)b(.*)c(.*)d, DOTALL) for literal tokens
+    # -> (g1, g2, g3, match end). The regex backtracks quadratically over every
+    # a/b occurrence; greedy groups pick the last feasible d, then c, then b.
+    start = text.find(a)
+    d_pos = text.rfind(d)
+    if start == -1 or d_pos == -1:
+        return None
+    c_pos = text.rfind(c, 0, d_pos)
+    if c_pos == -1:
+        return None
+    b_pos = text.rfind(b, start + len(a), c_pos)
+    if b_pos == -1:
+        return None
+    return (
+        text[start + len(a) : b_pos],
+        text[b_pos + len(b) : c_pos],
+        text[c_pos + len(c) : d_pos],
+        d_pos + len(d),
+    )
+
+
+def _iter_call_blocks(text: str):
+    # Linear scan for `begin.*?end` blocks; a regex rescans to the end from every
+    # begin token when the end token never arrives.
+    start = text.find(_CALL_BEGIN)
+    while start != -1:
+        end = text.find(_CALL_END, start + len(_CALL_BEGIN))
+        if end == -1:
+            return
+        end += len(_CALL_END)
+        yield start, end
+        start = text.find(_CALL_BEGIN, end)
+
+
